title: The Self-Existence of God
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The self-existence of God means that God depends on nothing outside Himself for life, being, power, or purpose. He is the eternal I AM, possessing life in Himself and giving life to all creation.
summary: The self-existence of God means that God depends on nothing outside Himself for life, being, power, or purpose. He is the eternal I AM, possessing life in Himself and giving life to all creation.
christFocus: Jesus Christ shares divine life with the Father and gives life to His people. In Him, sinners do not meet a needy deity, but the self-existent Lord who freely gives eternal life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God is not sustained by creation. He does not need the world, human service, worship, power, or approval in order to exist. He is the I AM, the One who has being in Himself.

Every creature depends on God, but God depends on no creature. He gives life, breath, and all things, yet He is not served by human hands as though He lacked something. His life is eternal, independent, and full.

The self-existence of God also means that His love and grace are free. God does not create, save, or draw near because He is empty or lonely. He acts from the fullness of His own goodness and purpose.

This doctrine humbles human pride and strengthens worship. The God who needs nothing has chosen to make Himself known and give life to those who have nothing apart from Him.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often imagine God as though He is like them: needy, dependent, insecure, or incomplete. Scripture reveals a God who is infinitely full in Himself and yet freely generous toward His creatures.

This doctrine gives rest. God’s faithfulness is not fragile because He is not held together by anything outside Himself. The One who gives life is never in danger of losing His own.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Depend on God without imagining that He depends on you. Serve Him gratefully, not as though He is needy, but because He is worthy. Receive life, breath, grace, and purpose as gifts from the self-existent Lord revealed in Christ.
